record.field: Changes effective July 1, 2026, Newfoundland and Labrador; step 4, K1P; table 8.2

Basic personal amount raised from 11,188 to 13,094 for 2026; since the pays of the first half used 11,188, a prorated 15,000 applies from the first pay of July. An employee who filed a TD1NL with the lower amount before July 1 needs no new form. Brackets and constants unchanged.

Newfoundland and Labrador rates 8.7%, 14.5%, 15.8%, 17.8%, 19.8%, 20.8%, 21.3% and 21.8% from 44,678, 89,354, 159,528, 223,340, 285,319, 570,638 and 1,141,275, constants KP; basic personal amount 11,188 (indexation 1.1%). No surtax, premium, reduction or labour-sponsored funds credit.
TD1NL 2026 Newfoundland and Labrador Personal Tax Credits Return
Line 1 (basic personal amount) and the total claim amount
Total claim amount TCP entered on the contract when the employee claims more than the basic personal amount.
Newfoundland and Labrador Department of Finance
Rates and brackets of the provincial personal income tax and the non-refundable credits: basic personal amount 11,067 for 2025 and 13,094 for 2026.
Bill 16, An Act to Amend the Income Tax Act, 2000
House of Assembly of Newfoundland and Labrador
Section 1 (basic personal amount) and section 5 (coming into force)
Basic personal amount of 13,094 for 2026, considered in force from January 1, 2026, not indexed before 2027; 15,000 indexed by the consumer price index for 2027.
Health and Post-Secondary Education Tax (Payroll Tax)
Newfoundland and Labrador Department of Finance

Tax of 2% payable by employers on the annual remuneration in the province above the exemption threshold, 2,000,000 for all employers since January 1, 2023. Associated employers and partners file an allocation agreement that shares the exemption.
Health and Post-Secondary Education Tax Return Explanation
Newfoundland and Labrador Department of Finance
Lines 1 to 4 of the monthly return

Remuneration: the amounts of employment income (Income Tax Act, s. 5(1), 6 and 7) of the employees who report for work in the province. The allocated deduction is reduced by the payroll of each period until it is exhausted; tax = 2% x (gross remuneration of the period - deduction left), at least 0. Return and payment within 20 days after the end of each month.
Revenue Administration Act, SNL 2009, c. R-15.01
House of Assembly of Newfoundland and Labrador
Part IV, s. 73 (tax of 2%); s. 2(w) (exemption threshold), 2(jjj) (remuneration), 2(qqq) (taxable remuneration), 2.01 (association)
Rate of 2% of the taxable remuneration; exemption of 2,000,000; a group of associated employers deducts the shares of its allocation agreement, and nothing without one.
House of Assembly of Newfoundland and Labrador
Monthly return and payment no later than 20 days after the end of the month; association fixed at the beginning of the calendar year.

Maximum assessable earnings per worker, adjusted each year by the consumer price index: 79,345 in 2025, 80,935 in 2026, 82,800 in 2027. Assessment = rate per $100 x assessable payroll; Employer Payroll Statement due February 28; excess earnings above the maximum deducted per worker; minimum annual assessment of 50.
